A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same M2S research work, including complete Appendices A–F. All 19 pages were compared; pages 2–19 match in extracted text and rendered appearance, with differences confined to the first-page title and header.

before.justification: v2 reports original M2S attack evaluations across four LLMs and a safeguard model, token-use measurements, and tactic analyses. Appendices B–C include original CoSafe and ATTACK_600 results.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results in Sections 4–5 and the appendices, including attack success, safeguard bypass, token usage, and tactic analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Hyphenize, Numberize, and Pythonize transformations, prompt templates, and single-turn response procedures. No algorithm or component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use MHJ, CoSafe, and ATTACK_600 for the same evaluations and token analyses, plus JailbreakBench for threshold validation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, 6, and 7 retain the same original multi-turn comparator and the same three M2S variants and ensemble. Comparator membership is unchanged in each experiment.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same models, evaluator, final-response evaluation, best-of-three aggregation, token-counting procedure, and metrics, including the 0.25 ASR threshold and 1.0 Perfect-ASR criterion.

E4.justification: The adoption-frequency, token-use, and tactic-specific analyses remain identical, including the score-increase, consistent-high-score, and score-drop categories in Appendix D. Appendix E retains the same usage example.

E5.justification: Both retain the 'single experiment' statement for each model in Section 4.2 and the token-count standard deviations in Table 4. No seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including Tables 1–10 and the appendix figures. For example, Table 1 reports GPT-4o ASRs of 71.5% for Original and 89.0% for Ensemble in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of multi-turn context and single-turn aggregation in Section 3 and the metric definitions in Section 4.3 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion are identical. Claims about systematic M2S conversion, attack effectiveness, token savings, and safeguard vulnerabilities retain the same meaning and scope despite the new title.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning contextual blindness, model-specific formatting preferences, and conversation-dependent tactics are unchanged. Section 7 retains all seven limitations and the same future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Both provide the same conversion templates, model and evaluator identifiers, tiktoken configuration, and data-release description in Section 5.6. The code/data repository link and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are identical. The title change does not revise the claimed relationship to prior jailbreak research.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'One-Shot is Enough: Consolidating Multi-Turn Attacks into Efficient Single-Turn Prompts for LLMs' to 'M2S: Multi-turn to Single-turn jailbreak in Red Teaming for LLMs'. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; all other prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new title occupies one line instead of two, shifting the author and affiliation block upward. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of pages 2–19 remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 changes the title and first-page header while preserving the methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, reproducibility information, and limitations throughout the main text and appendices. These limited presentation edits produce no meaningful net difference in scientific support, completeness, or overall paper quality.
